## Intent
Hypothesis: a Halide-expressible math walk over identity-ordered particles with no intermediates can approach the streaming bandwidth ceiling on low-churn workloads.

## Cache saturation
At q=0.01, ns/p falls from 12.219 at N=4000 to 8.343 at N=65000 as fixed overhead amortizes, then stays flat at 8.373 (N=262000) through the L2→DRAM spill at N≈61680 with no knee, rising only slightly to 8.78 at N=4000000. The same shape holds at q=0.05 (9.512→9.026→9.355) and q=0.25 (14.673→11.283→11.75): death rate raises the floor without altering the N-curve. The absence of any cost rise at the L2 spill confirms the algo is not cache-pressure-limited; the L1d spill at N≈963 is never directly sampled but its effect is subsumed into the overhead-amortization regime below N=65000.

## Bandwidth
Peak achieved is 8.15 GB/s at N=65000, q=0.01 — 32% of the 25.22 GB/s streaming ceiling. Bandwidth is essentially flat across N after amortization (8.15→7.74 GB/s at q=0.01), and death rate erodes it: peak drops to 7.53 GB/s (30%) at q=0.05 and 6.03 GB/s (24%) at q=0.25. The algo is overhead/compute-bound, not bandwidth-bound: flat ns/p with no DRAM knee means it never enters a streaming regime, and rising churn shifts it further into branchy-respawn cost.

## Assembly
The compiler did not vectorize: zero vector-suffixed instructions appear in the 345-insn step. All floating-point math is scalar — `fmul` (×4), `fadd`, `fsub` operate on `s` registers, and `ldp s5, s6` loads particle components as scalar pairs. The single `ldr q0` loads a constant, not particle data. The inner scatter loop uses byte-granular `ldrb`/`strb` sequences (e.g., `strb w2, [x1]`, `strb w2, [x1, #0x1]`, `strb w2, [x1, #0x2]`) with `csel` clamping to 0–255 and `fcvtzs` for float-to-int conversion. This scalar codegen with byte-scatter read-modify-writes explains the 32% ceiling: the byte stores cannot stream, and no SIMD parallelism is exploited over particles or components.

## Verdict
Refuted — the algo never exceeds 8.15 GB/s (32% of the 25.22 GB/s ceiling) at q=0.01, N=65000, and the compiler produced zero vectorized instructions. The byte-granular scatter stores and scalar-only math prevent any streaming regime, and death rate further erodes bandwidth to 6.03 GB/s (24%) at q=0.25. The Halide-expressible math walk does not translate into vectorized or bandwidth-saturating code.
